newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Navy calls off search for crashed helicopter.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Navy calls off search for crashed helicopter.

text.p: The U.S. Navy said on Saturday it had called off the search for one of its Seahawk helicopters, missing with four crewmen on board since crashing off the North Carolina coast late on Thursday night.
A spokesman for the Naval Air Station at Jacksonville, Fla., where the HH-60H aircraft was based, said he could not discuss whether the four crewmen were believed to have died.
"I don't have the status," he said. "I have no other information."

The Seahawk, operating off the aircraft carrier USS John F. Kennedy, crashed at about 11:30 p.m. EST (0435 GMT) on Thursday during a training exercise about 80 miles (130 km) off North Carolina. It crashed while attempting to refuel from a Navy frigate.
Neither the aircraft carrier nor frigate was involved in the crash, and no other personnel were injured.

Members of the missing crew were identified as pilots Lieut. Commander Joseph King of Orange Park, Fla. and Lieut. Christopher Buckley of Hampton, N.Y., and aircrewmen Chief Petty Office Andrew Baker of Middleburg, Fla., and Second Class Petty Officer Edward Kos of Jacksonville.
Navy and Coast Guard aircraft and sea vessels had searched for the missing men in extremely rough seas after the crash.
The Navy spokesman said the Navy was conducting an investigation into the cause of the crash.
